ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, signatories and beneficial principals against TRACFIN's national freezing list (décisions de gel under CMF Articles L.562-1 to L.562-6), EU consolidated financial sanctions lists (including Regulation (EU) 269/2014 and 2580/2001), UN Security Council sanctions, and, where the payment rails touch US dollars or US correspondent banks, the OFAC SDN list. Politically Exposed Persons are identified under the Sapin II / AMLD4 definition; enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification are mandatory where a PEP relationship, adverse media or unusual transaction pattern is detected.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) maintained by the greffe du tribunal de commerce and consulted via Infogreffe; formalities submitted through the official French one-stop company platform 'formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr' (guichet unique)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The RCS accepts and registers a corporate name written in Latin script; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into a Romanized equivalent in the statutes and French public filings. The name must be freely available in France, not confusingly similar to earlier RCS names or prior trademarks, not misleading as to the legal form or activity, and the statuts must be drafted in French under Article 2 of the French Constitution and the Toubon Law (Loi n° 94-665 of 4 August 1994, as amended).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In France, a corporate name is not formally 'pre-reserved'; availability is established at RCS registration. Upon refusal, the applicant must obtain the greffier's written grounds, then (1) re-file immediately with a corrected and differentiated name through the guichet unique; (2) if the same registrar refuses a second time, appeal by a simple declaration to the tribunal judiciaire of the company's registered office within one month of notification under Article L.123-16 of the Code de commerce, with the Ministère Public notified; (3) if the objection arises from an identical trademark, initiate an INPI opposition or cancellation action under Articles L.712-4 and L.716-4 of the Code de la propriété intellectuelle; (4) if the refusal relates to a reserved sensitive token, apply in parallel for the competent ministerial or regulatory authorization before resubmitting the name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A licensed commercial domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) may serve as the statutory registered office under Article L.123-11-2 of the Code de commerce, and this is commonly used for a French SAS. However, for an ISIC 3250 manufacturer of dental zirconia blocks and milling discs, a virtual mail-drop office is not sufficient commercial substance: the SAS must be able to demonstrate a physical registered establishment in France, or a binding contract manufacturer arrangement, together with retention of the EU MDR 2017/745 technical documentation, vigilance files and medical-device registration information at an address accessible to the ANSM, French customs, tax authorities and the notified body.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified institutional risk: 25-35% annual probability of an unannounced or planned inspection of the manufacturing/quality-management site by ANSM, the notified body, URSSAF or customs authorities; 5-10% annual probability for the French registered office if it is a licensed domiciliation address and all substantive files are held elsewhere.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), acting through the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE); corporate and VAT registration are initiated through the Guichet Unique operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI). Electronic portals: impots.gouv.fr (tax filing and VAT returns), formalites.entreprises.fr (entity and TIN registration), and douane.gouv.fr (customs and export declarations).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS obtains its statutory tax identification number (numéro SIREN/SIRET) automatically upon company incorporation via the Guichet Unique, which transmits the registration file to the INSEE and the DGFiP. The VAT intra-Community identification number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire, format FR + 2-digit key + 9-digit SIREN) is issued ex officio by the DGFiP after the INSEE registration is completed. A foreign entity without a French establishment but carrying out taxable transactions in France must apply directly to the DGFiP for a TIN/VAT number under Article 286 ter of the Code Général des Impôts (CGI); a non-established operator must in principle appoint an accredited fiscal representative in France under Article 289 A CGI, unless an EU simplification applies, and must provide proof of its foreign registration, identity documents of the legal representative, and a description of the intended French activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A French SAS is subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, Article 206-1 CGI) at entity level. It is not pass-through eligible by default, and its French corporate tax residence entails taxation of worldwide profits subject to tax-treaty relief and to the territoriality carve-out for foreign permanent establishments in certain treaty situations. France has no general check-the-box regime; the civil-law classification of the SAS as a limited-liability company is determinative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election exists for French entities. Available elective mechanisms include: (1) French tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI, allowing a French parent holding at least 95% of a French subsidiary to consolidate results, available to an SAS forming a group; (2) the option for the personal-income-tax/partnership regime under Article 239 bis AB CGI, available in narrow conditions only to SARL-type companies and certain family/SME entities, and not generally available to an SAS with non-individual shareholders; (3) the option for corporate income tax for entities that would otherwise be taxed as partnerships; (4) the VAT group (assujetti unique) election under Article 256 C CGI once the relevant administrative authorisation is obtained; and (5) hybrid-mismatch filing and documentation obligations under Articles 212 bis B and 212 bis C CGI, which require calibrated elections and contemporaneous transfer-pricing evidence for cross-border related-party transactions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA, Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée), governed by Articles 256 to 289 E CGI and Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold triggers VAT registration in France: any person independently carrying out a taxable economic activity is liable for VAT from the first taxable transaction. The statutory small-business exemption (franchise en base de TVA, Article 293 B CGI) applies only to established taxable persons whose preceding calendar-year turnover does not exceed EUR 91,900 for supplies of goods or EUR 36,800 for services (with reduced thresholds where the activity comprises a service component above EUR 10,000); a manufacturing SAS selling dental zirconia blocks to dental laboratories and professionals will not benefit from the exemption if it opts to invoice VAT or if it exceeds the threshold, and in any event the exemption is not available for enterprises formed as SAS unless they are in their first year of activity and meet the statutory ceilings.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is transitioning to mandatory B2B electronic invoicing and e-reporting through the Reforme de la Facturation Electronique. The implementation timeline is phased: large and mid-sized enterprises must issue and receive structured e-invoices from 1 September 2026, and SMEs from 1 September 2027. Electronic invoices must be transmitted through an immatriculated Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP) or through the free Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) using structured formats such as Factur-X, UBL, or CII/EN 16931. Transaction and invoice data are compulsorily transmitted to the DGFiP for VAT control, thereby creating a continuous transaction control environment comparable to real-time clearance, although France does not use a fiscal stamping or pre-clearance system. Customs export operations are declared in real-time via DELTA-X through the Guichet Unique National (GUN), and intra-EU goods flows require DES/Intrastat declarations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible movable goods physically leaving France and the European Union are exempt from French VAT with credit for input VAT under Article 262-I CGI (true export). To claim the exemption, the SAS must prove: (i) transfer of the power to dispose of the goods in its capacity as supplier; (ii) actual and decisive removal of the goods from EU customs territory within the statutory or administrative timeframe, supported by a customs export declaration (régime douanier 1000) accepted by French customs via DELTA-X and the official exit certificate (preuve d'exportation, typically the Bill of Lading, airway bill, or CMR coupled with an electronic exit record); (iii) compliance with the 90-day administrative deadline for the goods to leave the Union; and (iv) retention of a complete documentary file in France. If the dental zirconia blocks are sold to a taxable customer established in another EU member state, the transaction is classified as an intra-Community supply exempt under Article 262 ter I CGI, which additionally requires the customer's valid VAT number, the inclusion of the sale in the EC Sales List (déclaration d'échanges de biens), and delivery to the customer in that member state.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'Exportation, DELTA-X format, customs procedure code 1000) accepted by French customs and the export exit record
Bill of Lading (connaissement), airway bill, CMR, or multimodal transport document showing the goods leaving France/EU territory
Commercial invoice with full Incoterms and export references, together with the purchase order or sales contract
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank credit evidence (SWIFT MT103/MT950 or attestation de domiciliation bancaire) proving settlement of the export payment
Proof of arrival or customs entry in the destination country, where available, and VAT registration data of the customer for intra-EU supplies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP may reopen the export exemption position for the standard three-year prescription period, extended to six years where the taxpayer has failed to file returns or has engaged in an activity designed to dissimulate taxable operations. Any deficiency in the export proof file triggers the reversal of the zero rating and the assessment of the 20% TVA on the export sales, plus intérêts de retard (0.20% per month). If the deficiency is held to result from bad faith or abusive behaviour, a major penalty of 40% or 80% is applied under Article 1729 CGI, and fraudulent export schemes can lead to the 80% fraud penalty together with criminal prosecution under Article 1741 CGI, carrying a fine of up to EUR 500,000 and five years' imprisonment for legal representatives found personally responsible. In parallel, the customs administration may apply Code des Douanes penalties, including confiscation and fines equal to one to two times the value of the proceeds. The input VAT allocated to the zero-rated exports is correspondingly clawed back, and any artificial arrangements at the level of the export customer or intermediary may be recharacterised under abuse of law rights (abus de droit) and subjected to the same sanctions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, operating as the national central bank within the Eurosystem and in conjunction with the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) for banking supervision and compliance; exchange-control and balance-of-payments reporting duties are exercised by Banque de France under the French Code monétaire et financier and EU treaty provisions on the free movement of capital.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a Eurozone member and an IMF Article VIII participant, therefore the euro is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions. There is no blanket administrative approval requirement for cross-border payments. Profit and dividend remittances from a French SAS are operationally free after the legal corporate formalities, audited financial statements and tax clearances; the bank will only apply sanctions screening, AML/KYC checks, and the compulsory balance-of-payments statistical reporting. For non-EEA capital transactions, France retains the right to impose temporary safeguard measures or request statistical declarations on large transactions, and investment in sensitive defence/security sectors may require prior authorisation under the French foreign-investment screening regime, but these do not represent normal convertibility restrictions on dental consumables manufacturing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no mandatory surrender of export proceeds and no forced conversion into euro. Exporters are free to maintain foreign-currency settlement accounts and retain export earnings. However, all French resident exporters and, in substance, their financing banks are subject to Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting: any cross-border payment or collection reaching or exceeding EUR 150,000 per transaction requires an individual declaration, while transactions between EUR 10,000 and EUR 150,000 are reported on an aggregated basis through the intermediary. The exporter must retain supporting documentation (export declaration, commercial invoice, transport documents, cash receipt evidence) for a minimum of five years; failure to furnish accurate declarations can give rise to administrative fines and delays in clearing inbound export remittances.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) and Operational Multi-Currency Current Account
Operational Current Account with SWIFT, Trade Finance, and Foreign Exchange Hedging Facilities
Operational Current Account and Export Settlement Account for Trade Flows
Operational Current Account and Cash Pooling Arrangement for Group Liquidity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium only where the electronic-money or payment institution is EEA-licensed under PSD2 and registered in France with ACPR or is a properly appointed agent of an ACPR-registered institution; in such cases a virtual IBAN and digital treasury dashboard can be used for collection of dental-lab receivables and supplier payments. Low for offshore, non-EEA EMIs or 'quick-IBAN' providers, as they cannot maintain a direct Banque de France relationship, cannot open true French current accounts, and are generally unwilling to support documentary trade or FX hedging. Therefore fintech EMIs are acceptable only as a supplementary receivables-collection rail and must never be the sole repository for the French SAS corporate treasury, capital escrow, or VAT/tax settlement amounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under ACPR AML/CTF rules, the key legal representative and beneficial owners must undergo reliable customer identification through physical appearance or a recognised remote video-identification process with live document inspection. Remote-only account opening is legally possible in France but is accepted in practice only where the bank already holds an e-KYC technology approval; for a newly incorporated SAS with foreign shareholders and low historical track record, banks will normally require the President and a director to appear physically or to have their identity apostilled and consularised through the local embassy. A statutory interview concerning source of funds, commercial purpose, expected cross-border turnover, and beneficial ownership will be commanded before granting access to trade finance, foreign exchange lines, and SWIFT payment factories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner resides in a high-risk/FATF-grey-listed jurisdiction or appears in adverse political-exposure databases
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete corporate KYC file: notarised and apostilled shareholder registry, certified passport pages of all natural persons, a lawful ownership chart to final natural persons, principal source-of-wealth report, French residential or business presence proof, a letter of reference from the current sponsoring bank, an auditor's or expert-comptable's AML opinion, and a sanctions/terrorism radar clearance certificate from the French Direction Générale du Trésor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial paid-in share capital is injected in large currency amounts from a non-EEA parent company without operating history, creating suspected channel/straw-man funding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements of the sending corporate account for at least 12 months, audited financial statements of the parent for the past two years, board resolution authorising the capital contribution, underlying commercial contracts for the dental ceramic powder/milling machine supply, source-of-funds declaration signed by the CFO, and a notarial or bank capital-deposit certificate showing the specific contribution was held in the French SAS blocked account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The dental product scope falls under regulated medical-device activities, which can theoretically disguise trade-based money laundering or over-invoicing for fictitious dental imports/exports
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French ANSM (National Agency for Medicines and Health Products Safety) establishment registration, CE marking certificate under Regulation (EU) 2017/745, ISO 13485 certificate, technical file and IFU, EUDAMED registration extract, detailed purchase orders from dental laboratories, shipping bills of lading/AWB, customs declarations, and transactional evidence trails tying each invoice to a physically delivered zirconia block.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections into the French SAS must be executed by a priority SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 cover) with the French IBAN and the investing bank's BIC embedded. The payment must be accompanied by a purpose code corresponding to 'Investissement direct – capital et réserves' according to the Banque de France balance-of-payments nomenclature, and the receiving bank must hold the following verification batch: the constitutional corporate deeds of the SAS, the capital-subscription resolution, the French bank or notary deposit certificate, the origin-of-funds declaration, the personal identification of beneficial owners, and a tax-status statement confirming no inconsistent profit-shifting. Receipts greater than EUR 150,000 automatically generate a Banque de France BOP report, and wire clarity must be maintained by avoiding reference to general fiduciary accounts or crypto-linked channels. When the capital is received in a foreign currency, Banque de France permits credit to a euro-denominated account only after conversion by the receiving bank, which must retain the FX contract for audit trail.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement from the French operational account should prioritise the following clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for T/T wires to non-SEPA destinations and for settlement against dental laboratory invoices; (2) SEPA Credit Transfer via TARGET2 for intra-EU payments, with no purpose code but structured creditor reference; (3) documentary commercial LC operations through SWIFT MT700/MT710/MT720 channels under UCP600 for substantial buyer-initiated imports or exports; (4) local clearing for high-volume low-value payments in markets where B2B customers require ACH/Paynet-style rails. Each disbursement must be tied to an underlying invoice, customs declaration, or freight document, and must pass in real time through the bank's sanctions and counterparty filter. Foreign-exchange spot conversion at the time of payment must be evidenced by a spot dealing ticket, and all non-euro creditor payments must be recorded with the Banque de France BOP reporting trigger to enable seamless reconciliation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot EUR/FX contracts for current trade settlement
Outright EUR/CNY or EUR/USD forward contracts with tenors up to 24 months supported by underlying commercial receivables or payables
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with limited convertibility, e.g. EUR/CNH or EUR/BRL, while respecting hedge-accounting documentation
Cross-currency swaps under an ISDA/CSA framework for redenominating future dental-lab receivables into euro
Vanilla FX options (call/put) purchased for hedging bi-directional trade exposure with a cap on premium
Exchange-traded currency futures and options listed on Euronext or the London Stock Exchange derivatives market for corporations qualifying as professional counterparties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual approval of SAS financial statements and deposit of annual accounts (Dépôt des comptes annuels) including profit appropriation and management declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must approve accounts within six months of financial year-end; deposit with the registry within one month after approval. For a calendar-year SAS: approval by 30 June and filing by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The President (Président) faces criminal fine up to EUR 9,000 for failure to file accounts within deadline; the court may order sequestration of accounts or impose an injunctive penalty payment; repeated default can result in registration of insolvency flags and, after formal demand, administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and financial statements annex (Liasse Fiscale: déclaration de résultats n° 2065 and n° 2050-series schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year French GAAP accounts: file by the second working day after 1 May, with an online-filing extension generally to 15 May; for a non-calendar year-end: file within three months of fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of the unpaid tax (5% if formally regularised spontaneously before notification); late-payment interest (intérêt de retard) applies monthly at 0.20%; after formal demand and non-payment, the penalty rises to 40% (80% for abusive concealment) and tax lien procedures may be initiated.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-ownership declaration update (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) – filed at RCS upon incorporation and within 30 days after any change of shareholders or beneficial owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No fixed annual calendar deadline; update must be filed within 30 days following any transfer of shares or change in beneficial-ownership chain.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is punishable by a criminal fine of up to EUR 7,500 for a legal entity (and up to EUR 15,000 in case of repeated offence); the court may also order publication of the judgment and the registry may refuse further filings until the declaration is regularised.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A French SAS must appoint a statutory auditor (Commissaire aux Comptes) if it exceeds two of the following three thresholds at the financial year-end: total balance-sheet assets greater than EUR 4 million, net turnover greater than EUR 8 million, and an average headcount of more than 50 employees. An auditor is also mandatory when the SAS is a parent of subordinate companies regardless of size under group-audit rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French local GAAP (Plan Comptable Général – PCG; ANC Règlement n° 2014-03) for the statutory individual financial statements; EU-endorsed IFRS for consolidated accounts if the SAS heads a group and is required to prepare consolidated accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not impose a separate annual UBO confirmation return. Beneficial-ownership data is filed with the RCS at incorporation and must be voluntarily updated within 30 days after any transfer of shares or other change in beneficial ownership. The annual accounts filing does not re-validate UBO data; however, the Greffe may periodically require updated confirmation during registry audits or when other filings are made.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shareholders and Securities Movements (Registre des actionnaires et des mouvements de titres)
Register of Corporate Decisions / Minutes (Registre des décisions / procès-verbaux)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 150 to EUR 900 per year (approximately USD 165 to USD 990) for a domiciliation provider or registered-office service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 4,000 to EUR 15,000 per audit (approximately USD 4,400 to USD 16,500), varying with entity size and complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on first €42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs (turnover < €10M); Research Tax Credit (CIR) up to 30% of eligible R&D expenses; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) for SMEs; territorial deduction for intangible assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed via EFI (Échange de Formulaires Informatisés) on impots.gouv.fr; accompanying schedules 2050-2059.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending 31 December, filing deadline is 3 May of the following year; for other year-ends, within 3 months of year-end. Quarterly advance payments (acomptes) due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit after adjustments (reintegration of non-deductible expenses, deduction of tax credits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a French permanent establishment (PE) must file the same form; if no PE but French-source income, use Form 2065-SD (simplified) or specific withholding forms.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carryforward amount applied to current year profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses from French PE can be carried forward subject to same rules; non-residents without PE cannot claim losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (CIR, CII, foreign tax credits) reducing tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may claim treaty credits if applicable; must attach Form 2069-RCI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed corporate income tax after credits and prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents subject to withholding tax on certain income; final tax due via Form 2571.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% surcharge on tax due (5% if filed within 30 days of deadline); monthly 0.5% interest on unpaid tax; additional 40% penalty for deliberate understatement, 80% for fraud.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% (standard rate for non-residents; 25% for EU/EEA residents under Parent-Subsidiary Directive if conditions met)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced DTA rate, non-resident must provide a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from home jurisdiction, submit Form 5000 (or 5001 for individuals) to the French tax authority, and file a claim with the dividend payer before payment. For EU/EEA, Form 5000 is replaced by a simplified attestation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 33.33% (but reduced to 0% under EU Interest & Royalties Directive if beneficial owner is EU resident; treaty rates typically 0-10%). Interest: statutory 30% (treaty rates often 0-15%; EU directive may exempt).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if annual turnover ≥ €50 million or if related-party transactions exceed €1 million; Master File required if group consolidated turnover ≥ €750 million.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies anti-abuse rules (e.g., substance-over-form, GAAR) and requires genuine economic activity for tax residency and treaty benefits. No separate ESR regime, but French tax authorities scrutinize shell companies and artificial arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable profit, false invoicing, or concealment of foreign bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 40% penalty on understated tax (80% for fraud), plus 0.40% monthly interest; criminal prosecution possible with fines up to €500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly liable for corporate tax debts if they participated in fraudulent acts; travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SAS with no real business activity, no employees, no premises, or artificial arrangements to shift profits to low-tax jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of transactions, denial of treaty benefits, 100% penalty on unreported income, and potential criminal charges for abuse of law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally assessed for unpaid taxes if they knowingly used the entity as a sham; travel bans and seizure of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Money laundering through corporate accounts, failure to declare beneficial owners (BO), or non-compliance with French AML obligations (e.g., no KYC procedures).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million for companies, imprisonment up to 5 years for individuals; confiscation of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can face criminal liability, including imprisonment and personal fines; travel bans and prohibition from managing companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain TP documentation, or pricing transactions with related parties not at arm's length, leading to profit shifting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, 40% penalty on additional tax, and interest; possible double taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for penalties if they knowingly approved non-compliant TP policies; personal fines and potential criminal prosecution.
